sentiment.rationale: The document reports a beat on both revenue ($22.4B vs ~$21.9B expected) and EPS ($0.41 vs ~$0.35-$0.37 expected), with auto margins improving sequentially from 17.9% to 19.2%. However, the margin improvement was helped by ~$230M of warranty true-downs, energy storage deployments fell 38% sequentially, and forward guidance includes negative free cash flow for the rest of the year with capex above $25B. The forward outlook is mixed: EMEA demand is surging and order backlog is the highest in over two years, but the company frames 2026 as a transition year and unsupervised FSD is pushed to Q4. The score is positive but tempered by the mixed quality of the beat and cautious forward guidance.

summary.guidance: 2026 capex above $25B, with negative free cash flow expected for the rest of the year. Unsupervised FSD framed as probably a fourth-quarter event. A transition year on the company's own framing.
summary.margin: Auto margins excluding credits 19.2%, up from 17.9%, helped by about $230M of warranty true-downs. Energy storage at a 39.5% gross margin including about $250M of tariff benefits.
key_risks: Battery pack capacity called the biggest limiter on production growth.
Negative free cash flow through 2026 during the investment phase.
Robotaxi complexity issues, including vehicles behaving over-cautiously and expansion limited beyond Texas cities.
Hardware 3 does not have the capability to achieve unsupervised FSD.
key_opportunities: EMEA deliveries surged, with France and Germany up over 150% quarter over quarter.
Highest Q1 order backlog in over two years.
Optimus will be our biggest product... probably the biggest product ever.

management_tone.label: mixed
management_tone.justification: Management highlights a beat and strong EMEA demand but also guides to negative free cash flow and frames 2026 as a transition year, creating a balanced but cautious tone.
